question: What is ophthalmia neonatorum?

options.A: A congenital defect of the retina present from early pregnancy
options.B: A severe eye infection acquired by a newborn during birth
options.C: A fungal infection of the inner ear canal in neonates
options.D: A normal eye discharge seen in all babies after crying

explanation: Ophthalmia neonatorum is an acute eye infection contracted when a baby passes through an infected birth canal. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T3#BMP213_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why do gonococcal eye infections appear earlier than chlamydial infections in newborns?

options.A: Chlamydia organisms hide inside maternal cells for months before birth
options.B: The newborn immune system selectively attacks chlamydia first
options.C: Gonorrhea bacteria are larger and block tear ducts immediately
options.D: Neisseria gonorrhoeae has a faster incubation period than Chlamydia trachomatis

explanation: Gonorrhea causes symptoms within a few days of birth due to its rapid growth rate, whereas chlamydia takes longer to incubate. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T3#BMP213_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of giving tetracycline eye ointment to a newborn?

options.A: To lubricate dry eyes caused by bright delivery room lights
options.B: To treat an existing congenital cataract in the infant
options.C: To speed up the opening of closed eyelids after birth
options.D: To prevent bacterial eye infections acquired during delivery

explanation: Tetracycline is given routinely right after birth to prevent infections like gonococcal conjunctivitis from developing. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T3#BMP213_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why is 1% tetracycline ointment preferred over older agents like silver nitrate?

options.A: It is completely absorbed into the bloodstream to cure systemic infections
options.B: It changes color when an infection is present to warn the midwife
options.C: It causes much less chemical irritation to the newborn's eyes
options.D: It does not require any prescription from a medical doctor

explanation: Silver nitrate frequently caused severe chemical conjunctivitis, whereas tetracycline is much gentler on newborn eyes. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T3#BMP213_U4_T3_h2)

question: When should prophylactic tetracycline ointment be administered to a newborn?

options.A: Only if the mother develops a fever
options.B: Within the first hour after delivery
options.C: After the baby completes the first week of life
options.D: Before the second stage of labor begins

explanation: Standard practice dictates giving the ointment shortly after birth while completing routine newborn care. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T3#BMP213_U4_T3_h3)

question: What should a midwife do immediately after applying the ointment to ensure even distribution?

options.A: Gently close the baby's eyelids to help spread the medication
options.B: Cover both eyes tightly with a heavy gauze bandage
options.C: Massage the eyeball firmly in a circular motion
options.D: Flush the eye immediately with warm saline solution

explanation: Closing the eye gently helps distribute the ointment across the surface without damaging the delicate tissue. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T3#BMP213_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which of the following is a common, mild reaction after applying tetracycline eye ointment?

options.A: Heavy bleeding from the tear ducts
options.B: Complete loss of the blink reflex
options.C: Transient redness and mild blurring of vision

explanation: Temporary irritation and mild redness are normal and typically clear up within a day or two. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T3#BMP213_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why is it important to reassure mothers about expected mild reactions to tetracycline?

options.A: To prevent unnecessary panic and premature attempts to wash the eyes
options.B: To encourage the mother to apply more ointment at home
options.C: To prove that the midwife is qualified to prescribe drugs
options.D: To ensure the mother pays for replacement medication

explanation: Knowing that mild redness is normal stops mothers from panicking or trying unprescribed remedies that could harm the baby. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T3#BMP213_U4_T3_h4)

question: What specific detail regarding the medication must be recorded in the baby's chart?

options.A: The market price of the tetracycline tube
options.B: The exact weight of the empty tube after use
options.C: The batch number and exact time of administration
options.D: The name of the pharmaceutical company's CEO

explanation: Recording batch numbers and timing ensures proper tracking and accountability in clinical care. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T3#BMP213_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why is accurate documentation of eye prophylaxis crucial in neonatal nursing?

options.A: It prevents the mother from asking questions about the baby
options.B: It provides a clear legal record that preventative care was completed
options.C: It guarantees the infant will never develop any eye disease
options.D: It allows the pharmacy to restock supplies automatically

explanation: Proper charting serves as legal evidence that standard prophylactic protocols were correctly executed. [learn more](BMP213_U4_T3#BMP213_U4_T3_h5)
